steps.instruction: The user request is: 'Add a button that clears every movie whose seen flag is true from the watchlist.' In this codebase the 'seen' flag is the existing WatchItem.watched boolean. Add a public method clearWatched(): void to WatchlistStore that: (1) removes every item with watched === true from the items signal, (2) leaves unwatched items in their current relative order, (3) persists the resulting list to localStorage exactly like the existing mutating methods (add/remove/toggleWatched) already do, and (4) keeps items, count and watchedCount consistent after the call. Calling it when no item is watched must be a safe no-op that leaves state unchanged. The watchlist component will call this method in this same round, so keep the exact name and signature clearWatched(): void. Do not change any existing exported behaviour; add your own tests for clearWatched in your spec file. If an existing test would have to change to accommodate this, do not change it silently - surface the conflict instead.

Add a 'Clear watched' button to the watchlist view that removes every watched movie from the watchlist. Requirements: (1) The button is a real <button> element with visible label 'Clear watched' and the attribute data-testid="clear-watched"; it is always rendered in the watchlist view (never hidden, e.g. not wrapped in an @if). (2) It is disabled while the watched count is 0 and enabled as soon as at least one movie is watched (bind [disabled] to watchedCount() === 0). (3) Clicking it calls a new component method clearWatched(): void that captures the current watched count, calls this.store.clearWatched(), and then sets announcement to a short non-empty message reflecting how many watched movies were removed, e.g. 'Removed 3 watched movies from your watchlist.' Cross-unit note: WatchlistStore is gaining the method clearWatched(): void in this same round; it removes all watched items from the store and persists them, so you only need to call it. Do not change or remove existing tests; add your own tests for the new button in your spec file. If an existing test would have to change to accommodate the button, do not change it silently - surface the conflict instead.

   remove(movie: WatchItem) {

   }
+
+  // Bulk action: drop every watched movie in one go. The count is captured before
+  // the store is emptied so the announcement can say how many entries were removed.
+  clearWatched(): void {
+    const removed = this.watchedCount()
+    this.store.clearWatched()
+    this.announcement.set(
+      removed === 1
+        ? 'Removed 1 watched movie from your watchlist'
+        : `Removed ${removed} watched movies from your watchlist`
+    )
